# Platform settings · Gateway

## Retries

<a id="RetryTimes"></a>

### Retries

Key `RetryTimes` · Type int · Range 0– · Default `2`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Retries

How many other channels a failed request is tried on before the caller gets the error. Rate limits, upstream 5xx errors, rejected keys and exhausted balances are retried; invalid requests (most 400s), 408 timeouts, the gateway's own errors and requests pinned to one channel are not. The retries never exceed the channels that serve the model and stop once the retry time limit has passed. 0 returns the first failure.

Examples:

- `2` A request to a model served by 5 channels is tried on at most 3 of them (the first plus 2 retries).
- `5` With only 2 channels serving the model, the request is tried on both and then fails: retries stop when no untried channel is left.
- `0` No retry: the first failure is returned to the caller.

See also: [Retry time limit](./gateway.md#RetryTimeOut) · [Rate limit cooldown](./gateway.md#RetryCooldownSeconds) · [Do not move a session on failure](./gateway.md#SessionAffinityStrict)

<a id="RetryCooldownSeconds"></a>

### Rate limit cooldown

Key `RetryCooldownSeconds` · Type int · Unit seconds · Range 0– · Default `5`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Retries

How long a channel is kept away from a model after it answers that model with a 429 rate limit. While it cools down, new requests for the model go to other channels; its other models are not affected. When the upstream says when the limit resets, that time is used instead. With supply pause rules on, this is the pause of the built-in rate_limit rule (custom rules carry their own seconds); with them off, a status code listed under per-status cooldowns takes precedence. 0 only skips the channel for the failed request.

Examples:

- `5` After a 429 for gpt-4o, that channel takes no gpt-4o requests for 5 seconds; it keeps serving its other models.
- `60` A channel with a per-minute limit sits out the rest of the minute instead of collecting more 429s.
- `0` No cooldown: the next request may land on the same channel and hit the limit again.

See also: [Per-status cooldown](./gateway.md#RetryCooldownPerStatus) · [Supply pause rules](./gateway.md#PauseRulesEnabled) · [Custom pause rules](./gateway.md#PauseRules)

<a id="RetryTimeOut"></a>

### Retry time limit

Key `RetryTimeOut` · Type int · Unit seconds · Range 0– · Default `10`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Retries

No new retry starts once this many seconds have passed since the request arrived. It is checked before each retry and does not cut an attempt that is already running, so long generations still finish. When it stops the retries, the caller gets a 503 saying the upstream is at capacity. 0 starts no retry at all.

Examples:

- `10` A first channel that fails after 12 seconds is not retried; one that fails after 3 seconds is, as long as the 10 seconds are not used up.
- `120` Suits long reasoning requests: a channel failing after a minute still leaves room for another try.

See also: [Retries](./gateway.md#RetryTimes)

<a id="RetryCooldownPerStatus"></a>

### Per-status cooldown

Key `RetryCooldownPerStatus` · Type json · Default `empty` · rarely changed

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Retries

Cooldowns in seconds for other HTTP status codes, as a JSON object of status code and seconds. Like the rate limit cooldown it keeps the channel away from that one model. With supply pause rules on, the built-in per_status rule applies it after the quota, credential, rate limit and model-not-found rules, so a 429 entry is never reached there, and a listed 5xx code no longer waits for three failures in a minute. With pause rules off, the order is the upstream's reset time, then this list, then the rate limit cooldown for 429. A code set to 0 is never cooled. Codes must be 100-599 and seconds whole numbers of 0 or more; empty adds none.

Examples:

- `{"503": 120}` A channel answering a model with 503 takes no requests for it for 2 minutes, from the first 503 on.
- `{"502": 60, "504": 300}` 502 cools the model on that channel for 1 minute, 504 for 5 minutes.
- `{"500": 0}` A 500 never pauses or cools the channel: the request moves on and the next one may use it again.

See also: [Rate limit cooldown](./gateway.md#RetryCooldownSeconds) · [Custom pause rules](./gateway.md#PauseRules) · [Supply pause rules](./gateway.md#PauseRulesEnabled)

<a id="ModelNotFoundCooldownSeconds"></a>

### Model not found pause

Key `ModelNotFoundCooldownSeconds` · Type int · Unit seconds · Range 0– · Default `21600` · rarely changed

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Retries

How long a channel is kept away from a model after its upstream says the model does not exist. There is no field for it on this page: change it through the option API (PUT /api/option/). It covers errors such as "model not found", "does not exist" or "no endpoints found", but not when a 429 was seen in the same request. With supply pause rules on, it is the pause of the built-in model_not_found rule, which also notifies admins; custom rules carry their own seconds. 0 never pauses for it.

Examples:

- `21600` A channel that lost access to gpt-4.5 stays out of gpt-4.5 requests for 6 hours, then gets tried again.
- `600` A model that was only briefly missing upstream comes back after 10 minutes.
- `0` The channel stays in rotation and keeps failing requests for the model until it is removed from the channel.

See also: [Supply pause rules](./gateway.md#PauseRulesEnabled) · [Custom pause rules](./gateway.md#PauseRules) · [Rate limit cooldown](./gateway.md#RetryCooldownSeconds)

## Supply pause rules

<a id="PauseRulesEnabled"></a>

### Supply pause rules

Key `PauseRulesEnabled` · Type bool · Default `true`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Supply pause rules

Failed requests go through the pause rules, which pause a channel or one of its models and bring it back on their own. When off, the older handling applies instead: automatic channel disabling (if switched on), the rate limit and per-status cooldowns, and the model-not-found pause.

Examples:

- `true` A channel whose key is rejected is paused for an hour and resumes after a passing test, without anyone re-enabling it.
- `false` A rejected key disables the channel when automatic disabling is on, and it stays off until a channel test passes.

See also: [Custom pause rules](./gateway.md#PauseRules) · [Disable channels that can no longer serve](./gateway.md#AutomaticDisableChannelEnabled) · [Rate limit cooldown](./gateway.md#RetryCooldownSeconds)

<a id="PauseRules"></a>

### Custom pause rules

Key `PauseRules` · Type json · Default `empty`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Supply pause rules

A JSON array of pause rules that replaces the built-in rules as a whole; empty uses the built-in ones. Rules are tried in order and the first match decides, after the channel's own rules. A rule matches on any of status_codes, keywords (substrings of the error, "re:" for a regular expression), error_types or error_codes, plus the flags unusable, model_not_found, rate_limit_reset and per_status_config; times and window_seconds make it count matches first. action is "pause" (for seconds, on the whole channel or, by default, the model) or "retry" (move on without pausing). probe sends a test request before resuming and doubles the pause when it fails; notify tells admins. Pauses under a minute are kept in memory only. Saved rules carry their own seconds, so the rate limit and model-not-found settings no longer apply to them.

Examples:

- `[{"name":"quota","status_codes":[402],"keywords":["credit balance is too low"],"action":"pause","seconds":1800,"scope":"channel","probe":true,"notify":true,"category":"quota"}]` A 402 or a low-balance message pauses the whole channel for 30 minutes and notifies admins; a test request runs before it resumes, and a balance refresh that finds money ends the pause early.
- `[{"name":"overloaded","status_codes":[529],"times":2,"window_seconds":60,"action":"pause","seconds":300,"probe":true}]` Two 529s for one model on one channel within a minute pause that model there for 5 minutes; if the test before resuming fails, the next pause lasts 10 minutes.
- `[]` No rule: nothing is ever paused, a failing channel is only skipped for the request that failed.

See also: [Supply pause rules](./gateway.md#PauseRulesEnabled) · [Rate limit cooldown](./gateway.md#RetryCooldownSeconds) · [Per-status cooldown](./gateway.md#RetryCooldownPerStatus) · [Model not found pause](./gateway.md#ModelNotFoundCooldownSeconds) · [Disable keywords](./gateway.md#DisableChannelKeywords)

## Channel auto disable & recovery

<a id="AutomaticDisableChannelEnabled"></a>

### Disable channels that can no longer serve

Key `AutomaticDisableChannelEnabled` · Type bool · Default `false`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Channel auto disable & recovery

Disables a channel whose upstream says it can no longer serve, such as a rejected key or an empty balance. An exhausted quota, a disabled account or a disable keyword in the error count too. On live requests this only happens while supply pause rules are off; with them on, such errors pause the channel instead. Channel tests disable for these errors too, with or without pause rules. A disabled channel comes back only through a passing test with automatic recovery on, or by hand.

See also: [Re-enable channels that pass a test](./gateway.md#AutomaticEnableChannelEnabled) · [Disable keywords](./gateway.md#DisableChannelKeywords) · [Supply pause rules](./gateway.md#PauseRulesEnabled) · [Scheduled channel test](./gateway.md#ChannelTestMode)

<a id="AutomaticEnableChannelEnabled"></a>

### Re-enable channels that pass a test

Key `AutomaticEnableChannelEnabled` · Type bool · Default `true`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Channel auto disable & recovery

A channel that was disabled automatically is enabled again when it passes a channel test. The test is a test of all channels, scheduled or started by hand, and must answer within the maximum response time. Channels an admin disabled are never enabled again on their own. When off, every disabled channel waits for an admin.

See also: [Disable channels that can no longer serve](./gateway.md#AutomaticDisableChannelEnabled) · [Scheduled channel test](./gateway.md#ChannelTestMode) · [Maximum response time](./gateway.md#ChannelDisableThreshold)

<a id="ChannelDisableThreshold"></a>

### Maximum response time

Key `ChannelDisableThreshold` · Type float · Unit seconds · Range 0– · Default `5`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Channel auto disable & recovery

A channel test slower than this many seconds disables an enabled channel and keeps a disabled one off. It applies to tests of all channels (scheduled in the All channels mode, or started from the channels page), whether or not automatic disabling is on; live requests are never timed against it. 0 sets no limit.

Examples:

- `5` A channel that takes 7.3 seconds to answer the test request is disabled; one that answers in 2 seconds keeps serving.
- `30` Leaves slow reasoning models alone and only disables channels that hang.
- `0` Tests disable channels for errors only, never for slowness.

See also: [Scheduled channel test](./gateway.md#ChannelTestMode) · [Re-enable channels that pass a test](./gateway.md#AutomaticEnableChannelEnabled)

<a id="DisableChannelKeywords"></a>

### Disable keywords

Key `DisableChannelKeywords` · Type list

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Channel auto disable & recovery

Error messages, one per line, that mark a channel as unable to serve when an upstream error contains one. Matching is case-sensitive, so copy the upstream text exactly; a keyword wins over the built-in exceptions. A match moves the request to another channel, pauses the channel through the built-in credential rule (1 hour, tested before resuming) with supply pause rules on, and disables it with them off and automatic disabling on. Empty leaves only the built-in checks of status codes and known messages.

Examples:

- `Your account is currently blocked` An upstream error containing this text pauses the whole channel for an hour instead of failing request after request.
- `Your credit balance is too low` Also matched by the built-in quota rule, which comes first: the channel pauses for 30 minutes and resumes early once a balance refresh finds money.

See also: [Disable channels that can no longer serve](./gateway.md#AutomaticDisableChannelEnabled) · [Custom pause rules](./gateway.md#PauseRules)

<a id="ChannelTestMode"></a>

### Scheduled channel test

Key `ChannelTestMode` · Type enum · Default `recovery`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Channel auto disable & recovery

Which channels the gateway tests on its own, every test interval. Each test is one small request to the channel's test model and is billed by the upstream. The CHANNEL_TEST_FREQUENCY environment variable, when set, overrides this: all channels every that many minutes.

Values:

- `recovery` Auto-disabled channels only: Tests only channels that were disabled automatically and, with automatic recovery on, enables those that pass; healthy channels spend nothing.
- `all` All channels: Tests every channel not disabled by hand: too slow ones are disabled, failing ones too when automatic disabling is on, and auto-disabled ones that pass come back.
- `off` Off: No scheduled test: disabled channels stay off until an admin tests or enables them.

See also: [Test interval](./gateway.md#ChannelTestIntervalMinutes) · [Re-enable channels that pass a test](./gateway.md#AutomaticEnableChannelEnabled) · [Maximum response time](./gateway.md#ChannelDisableThreshold)

<a id="ChannelTestIntervalMinutes"></a>

### Test interval

Key `ChannelTestIntervalMinutes` · Type int · Unit minutes · Range 1– · Default `10`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Channel auto disable & recovery

Minutes between two scheduled channel tests, at least one. A new interval applies from the next round, without a restart. Shorter intervals bring channels back sooner but send more test requests.

Examples:

- `10` An auto-disabled channel whose upstream recovered is back within about 10 minutes.
- `60` With All channels and 20 channels, 480 test requests a day.

See also: [Scheduled channel test](./gateway.md#ChannelTestMode)

<a id="ChannelCredentialRefreshMinutes"></a>

### Account credential refresh

Key `ChannelCredentialRefreshMinutes` · Type int · Unit minutes · Range 0– · Default `30` · rarely changed

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Channel auto disable & recovery

How often the OAuth credentials of Codex, Claude Code, Gemini CLI and Antigravity channels are checked. Credentials expiring before the next check (plus 15 minutes) are refreshed even on idle or auto-disabled channels, so they do not fail on their first request after a quiet night; channels disabled by hand are skipped. A channel whose refresh starts failing sends one channel credential notice. 0 turns the background refresh off.

Examples:

- `30` Every 30 minutes, tokens that expire within the next 45 minutes are renewed in the background.
- `0` No background refresh: a token can expire while its channel is idle.

## Error handling

<a id="ChannelFailErrorWrapEnabled"></a>

### Hide upstream errors

Key `ChannelFailErrorWrapEnabled` · Type bool · Default `true`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Error handling

Callers get a generic error instead of the upstream's own text, which may name the provider or show parts of a key. Upstream errors other than 400 become a 503 with the unified message (a 429 stays a 429 so clients back off), rejected channel keys get a fixed message, and a missing model a 404. 400 errors pass through, since they are about the request. Turn it off only for a while, to see what the upstream really says.

See also: [Unified error message](./gateway.md#ChannelFailErrorMessage)

<a id="ChannelFailErrorMessage"></a>

### Unified error message

Key `ChannelFailErrorMessage` · Type string · Default `Upstream for the current group is at capacity, please try again later`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Error handling

The message callers get when an upstream fails and upstream errors are hidden. The request id is added to it so a caller can quote it. Empty uses "Upstream for the current group is at capacity, please try again later". It has no effect while upstream errors are shown.

Examples:

- `Service busy, please retry in a minute` A failed request answers 503 with "Service busy, please retry in a minute (request id: ...)".

See also: [Hide upstream errors](./gateway.md#ChannelFailErrorWrapEnabled)

## Supply mode and cost

<a id="SupplyModeDefault"></a>

### Default supply mode

Key `SupplyModeDefault` · Type enum · Default `balance`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Supply mode and cost

How the supplies that take a model's requests share them, for models that follow the default. Only supplies that tie on priority (and on cost, see Cost and priority) share; a model can choose its own mode on its Supplies tab.

Values:

- `balance` Balance: Supplies of one tier share requests by weight.
- `failover` Failover: The heaviest supply of a tier takes every request; the others back it up.

Examples:

- `balance` Two supplies with weights 3 and 1 take about 75% and 25% of the requests.
- `failover` The supply with weight 3 takes every request; the one with weight 1 is used only while it fails.

See also: [Cost and priority](./gateway.md#SupplyCostOrder) · [Supply mode](./objects.md#model-supply_mode)

Guide: [use/pricing_and_routing.md#which-supply-takes-a-request](../use/pricing_and_routing.md#which-supply-takes-a-request)

<a id="SupplyCostOrder"></a>

### Cost and priority

Key `SupplyCostOrder` · Type enum · Default `priority`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Supply mode and cost

How far a supply's cost (its channel's list price with the channel's fee) moves it ahead. Users pay the catalog price times their group ratio either way; only your cost changes. Costs within 0.1% count as the same, and supplies of unknown cost come last.

Values:

- `priority` Priority first: Cost only orders supplies of the same priority.
- `cost` Cost first: The cheapest supplies of a model take the requests whatever their priority.

Examples:

- `priority` Requesty (cost x1.05) at the top priority keeps the requests of gpt-5.1; the official API (x1.00) one priority lower is its backup.
- `cost` The official API (x1.00) takes the requests of gpt-5.1; Requesty becomes a backup marked dearer.

See also: [Default supply mode](./gateway.md#SupplyModeDefault) · [Fee rate](./objects.md#channel-fee_rate) · [Priority](./objects.md#channel-priority)

Guide: [use/pricing_and_routing.md#which-supply-takes-a-request](../use/pricing_and_routing.md#which-supply-takes-a-request)

<a id="ModelSupplyEnabled"></a>

### Route by supplies

Key `ModelSupplyEnabled` · Type bool · Default `false` · rarely changed

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Supply mode and cost

Requests are routed through each public model's supplies instead of the channels' model lists and model mappings. There is no switch for it on this page: after migrating the channels to supplies (POST /api/model_supply/migrate, dry run first), turn it on through the option API (PUT /api/option/). While on, requests are billed by the public model, only published models are listed, and the supply mode, cost order, intake rules and pause rules decide where a request goes. Turning it off goes back to the channels' model lists at once and keeps the supplies.

Examples:

- `false` Requests follow each channel's models and model mapping; the supply pages only preview what would change.
- `true` A request for claude-sonnet-4-5 goes to the supplies of that public model, ordered by priority and cost.

See also: [Default supply mode](./gateway.md#SupplyModeDefault) · [Cost and priority](./gateway.md#SupplyCostOrder) · [Intake rules for new upstream models](./gateway.md#SupplyIntakeRules) · [Supply pause rules](./gateway.md#PauseRulesEnabled)

Guide: [use/supply_routing.md](../use/supply_routing.md)

## Intake rules for new upstream models

<a id="SupplyIntakeRules"></a>

### Intake rules for new upstream models

Key `SupplyIntakeRules` · Type json · Default `empty`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Intake rules for new upstream models

What happens to a model a channel's upstream starts listing, for channels that add new upstream models on their own. It is a JSON array tried from the top, and the first rule whose conditions all hold decides; a model no rule matches waits for review. Conditions: endpoints (abilities such as chat, responses, images, any of them), vendors (vendor ids), families and patterns (globs such as claude-* or *-preview*), supplied (whether another channel already supplies it). action is enable (routes at once), pending (added switched off until an admin confirms), disable (added switched off) or skip (not added). placement is auto (last when others already supply it), policy (where the allocation policy puts it) or last. Empty uses the built-in rules; saved rules replace them as a whole, and a channel can use rules of its own.

Examples:

- `[{"name":"Previews wait","patterns":["*-preview*","*-exp*"],"action":"pending"},{"name":"Chat joins","endpoints":["chat","responses"],"action":"enable","placement":"auto"},{"name":"Rest waits","action":"pending"}]` The built-in rules: gpt-5-preview waits for review, a new chat model routes at once (behind the channels that already supply it), an image model waits for review.
- `[{"name":"Claude joins","families":["claude-*"],"action":"enable","placement":"last"},{"name":"Rest skipped","action":"skip"}]` A new Claude model routes at once after the model's other supplies; any other new model is not added and stays in the list of new upstream models.

See also: [Route by supplies](./gateway.md#ModelSupplyEnabled) · [Default supply mode](./gateway.md#SupplyModeDefault)

## Session affinity

<a id="SessionAffinityEnabled"></a>

### Keep each session on one channel

Key `SessionAffinityEnabled` · Type bool · Default `true`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Session affinity

Requests of one client session go to the channel that served it first, so the upstream prompt cache keeps hitting. A session is recognised by the Claude Code session in metadata.user_id, a session header such as Codex's session_id, the OpenAI prompt_cache_key, or else the same system prompt and first user message. Claude Code, Gemini CLI and Codex account channels are always sticky, whatever this says. When off, each request is routed on its own.

See also: [Do not move a session on failure](./gateway.md#SessionAffinityStrict) · [Session lifetime](./gateway.md#SessionAffinityTTLSeconds) · [Add prompt cache markers](./gateway.md#ClaudePromptCachingEnabled)

<a id="SessionAffinityStrict"></a>

### Do not move a session on failure

Key `SessionAffinityStrict` · Type bool · Default `false`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Session affinity

When a session's channel fails, the caller gets the error instead of a retry on another channel. The channel is not paused for that model either (channel-wide pauses still apply). Moving loses the upstream prompt cache and the conversation state Codex keeps upstream. Errors that say the channel can no longer serve (a rejected key, an empty balance) still move the session. Leave it off to favour availability.

See also: [Keep each session on one channel](./gateway.md#SessionAffinityEnabled) · [Retries](./gateway.md#RetryTimes)

<a id="SessionAffinityTTLSeconds"></a>

### Session lifetime

Key `SessionAffinityTTLSeconds` · Type int · Unit seconds · Range 0– · Default `3600`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Session affinity

How long a session stays bound to its channel after its last request; every request starts the time again. Account channels (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex) always keep 1 hour. 0 uses 1 hour as well.

Examples:

- `3600` A coding session paused for 50 minutes comes back to the same channel; after 70 minutes it may land elsewhere.
- `300` Matches the upstream's 5-minute prompt cache: past that the cache is gone, so the session is free to move.

See also: [Keep each session on one channel](./gateway.md#SessionAffinityEnabled)

## Auto routing

<a id="RoutingDecisionBillingEnabled"></a>

### Charge the decision call

Key `RoutingDecisionBillingEnabled` · Type bool · Default `true`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Auto routing

Bills the call an auto routing policy makes to pick a model to the caller, at the decision model's price. It is charged once per session, as a log entry of its own. When off, the decision still runs, but the site pays for it and no consume log is written.

See also: [Own routing policies](./gateway.md#UserRoutingPolicyEnabled)

<a id="UserRoutingPolicyEnabled"></a>

### Own routing policies

Key `UserRoutingPolicyEnabled` · Type bool · Default `true`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Auto routing

Users and organizations can create routing policies of their own, called as policy/<name>. Users create personal policies under Routing policies in the workbench, organization owners and admins organization policies; an own policy overrides a platform policy of the same name for its own keys. When off, own policies are kept but no longer apply, and only platform policies resolve.

See also: [Policies per user](./gateway.md#PersonalRoutingPolicyMaxCount) · [Policies per organization](./gateway.md#OrganizationRoutingPolicyMaxCount)

<a id="PersonalRoutingPolicyMaxCount"></a>

### Policies per user

Key `PersonalRoutingPolicyMaxCount` · Type int · Range 0– · Default `20`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Auto routing

How many personal routing policies one user can create. Policies a user already has are kept when the cap is lowered; only new ones are refused. 0 sets no limit.

Examples:

- `20` A user with 20 policies gets an error when creating the 21st.
- `0` Users can create as many policies as they like.

See also: [Own routing policies](./gateway.md#UserRoutingPolicyEnabled) · [Policies per organization](./gateway.md#OrganizationRoutingPolicyMaxCount)

<a id="OrganizationRoutingPolicyMaxCount"></a>

### Policies per organization

Key `OrganizationRoutingPolicyMaxCount` · Type int · Range 0– · Default `20`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Auto routing

How many routing policies one organization can create. Policies it already has are kept when the cap is lowered; only new ones are refused. 0 sets no limit.

Examples:

- `20` An organization with 20 policies gets an error when creating the 21st.
- `5` Keeps organization policies few enough to review by hand.

See also: [Own routing policies](./gateway.md#UserRoutingPolicyEnabled) · [Policies per user](./gateway.md#PersonalRoutingPolicyMaxCount)

## Model name matching

<a id="ModelNameCaseInsensitiveEnabled"></a>

### Ignore case in model names

Key `ModelNameCaseInsensitiveEnabled` · Type bool · Default `false`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Model name matching

The model name a caller sends matches channels and prices whatever its case. When on, GPT-4o finds the channels and the price of gpt-4o, including wildcard prices. When off, names must match exactly and a differently cased name gets no channel.

See also: [Answer with the requested model name](./gateway.md#UnifiedRequestResponseModelEnabled)

<a id="UnifiedRequestResponseModelEnabled"></a>

### Answer with the requested model name

Key `UnifiedRequestResponseModelEnabled` · Type bool · Default `false`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Model name matching

The model field of every response carries the name the caller asked for, not the upstream model it was mapped to. Some clients check that the reply names the model they requested. When off, it is done only for channels and supplies that switch it on themselves.

Examples:

- `true` A request for my-chat mapped to gpt-4o-2024-08-06 answers with "model": "my-chat".
- `false` The same request answers with "model": "gpt-4o-2024-08-06", unless its channel or supply renames it.

See also: [Ignore case in model names](./gateway.md#ModelNameCaseInsensitiveEnabled) · [Pass upstream responses through](./gateway.md#FingerprintPassThroughEnabled)

## Native protocols

<a id="ClaudeAPIEnabled"></a>

### Claude Messages API

Key `ClaudeAPIEnabled` · Type bool · Default `true`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Native protocols

Callers can use the Anthropic Messages format (/claude/v1/messages and the coding agent endpoints) besides the OpenAI format. Claude Code and the Anthropic SDKs need it. When off, those endpoints answer 403 and llms.txt no longer lists them.

See also: [Gemini API](./gateway.md#GeminiAPIEnabled) · [Add prompt cache markers](./gateway.md#ClaudePromptCachingEnabled)

<a id="GeminiAPIEnabled"></a>

### Gemini API

Key `GeminiAPIEnabled` · Type bool · Default `true`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Native protocols

Callers can use the Google Gemini format (the /gemini/v1beta endpoints, Live API included) besides the OpenAI format. Gemini CLI and the Google SDKs need it. When off, those endpoints answer 403.

See also: [Claude Messages API](./gateway.md#ClaudeAPIEnabled) · [Show Gemini thoughts](./gateway.md#GeminiOpenThink)

<a id="ClaudePromptCachingEnabled"></a>

### Add prompt cache markers

Key `ClaudePromptCachingEnabled` · Type bool · Default `false`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Native protocols

Adds cache_control markers to requests for Anthropic models so the upstream caches the prompt. Later requests then read it at the cache price. It covers Claude, Opus, Sonnet and Haiku models on any channel type, and applies on channels whose prompt caching setting is Inherit; a channel set to On or Off decides for itself, along with the TTL and which messages are marked. Requests that already carry cache_control are left alone. Off by default.

Examples:

- `true` A client that sends no cache markers still gets its long system prompt cached upstream for 5 minutes.
- `false` Only clients that mark their prompts themselves, and channels set to On, use the cache.

See also: [Keep each session on one channel](./gateway.md#SessionAffinityEnabled) · [Claude Messages API](./gateway.md#ClaudeAPIEnabled)

<a id="FingerprintPassThroughEnabled"></a>

### Pass upstream responses through

Key `FingerprintPassThroughEnabled` · Type bool · Default `true` · rarely changed

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Native protocols

Keeps upstream responses as close to the original as possible. Non-streaming Claude and Bedrock responses are passed byte for byte, streams keep their model field, and upstream headers such as anthropic-ratelimit-*, x-ratelimit-* and x-amzn-* reach the caller. When off, responses are rebuilt like those of any other channel.

See also: [Answer with the requested model name](./gateway.md#UnifiedRequestResponseModelEnabled)

<a id="ClaudeBudgetTokensPercentage"></a>

### Default thinking budget

Key `ClaudeBudgetTokensPercentage` · Type float · Range 0–1 · Default `0.8`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Native protocols

The share of max_tokens Claude may spend thinking when a request asks for thinking without its own budget. It applies to OpenAI-format requests sent to Claude. budget_tokens = max_tokens x this value, and never below 1024. A request that names an effort gets 0.2, 0.5 or 0.8 for low, medium and high instead.

Examples:

- `0.8` With max_tokens 10000, Claude may think for 8000 tokens and has 2000 left for the answer.
- `0.5` With max_tokens 4096, the thinking budget is 2048 tokens.
- `0.1` With max_tokens 8192, 819 would be too small, so the budget is raised to 1024.

See also: [Default max tokens](./gateway.md#ClaudeDefaultMaxTokens)

<a id="ClaudeDefaultMaxTokens"></a>

### Default max tokens

Key `ClaudeDefaultMaxTokens` · Type json · Default `{"default":8192}`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Native protocols

The max_tokens sent to Claude when an OpenAI-format or Responses request sets no output limit. Claude requires one, so it is a JSON object of model name and tokens, with "default" for every other model. Requests that set max_tokens or max_completion_tokens keep their own. Empty means {"default": 8192}; an object without "default" leaves unlisted models without a limit and Claude rejects them, and text that is not valid JSON is ignored.

Examples:

- `{"default": 8192}` Every Claude request without a limit may write up to 8192 tokens.
- `{"default": 8192, "claude-sonnet-4-5": 64000}` claude-sonnet-4-5 requests without a limit may write up to 64000 tokens, other models 8192.

See also: [Default thinking budget](./gateway.md#ClaudeBudgetTokensPercentage)

<a id="GeminiOpenThink"></a>

### Show Gemini thoughts

Key `GeminiOpenThink` · Type json · Default `{}` · rarely changed

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Native protocols

Gemini models whose responses include their thought summaries, as a JSON object of model name and true. It only applies to models that can think; unlisted models keep thoughts out unless the request asks for them. Empty lists none, and text that is not valid JSON is ignored.

Examples:

- `{"gemini-2.5-pro": true}` gemini-2.5-pro replies carry the model's reasoning before the answer; gemini-2.5-flash replies do not.

See also: [Gemini API](./gateway.md#GeminiAPIEnabled)

## Prompt limits

<a id="MaxPromptTokens"></a>

### Max prompt tokens

Key `MaxPromptTokens` · Type int · Range 0– · Default `1000000` · rarely changed

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Prompt limits

Requests to AWS Bedrock channels with more input tokens than this are refused before reaching the upstream. They get a 400 "prompt is too long", which Claude Code reads like Anthropic's own; Bedrock would otherwise hang on them until its timeout. A model's context length in the catalog takes precedence; other channel types are not checked. 0 turns the check off.

Examples:

- `1000000` A 1.2 million token prompt to a Bedrock model with no context length in the catalog gets a 400 at once.
- `200000` Prompts over 200000 tokens are refused for Bedrock models without a known context length.

## Image proxy

<a id="ChatImageRequestProxy"></a>

### Image download proxy

Key `ChatImageRequestProxy` · Type url · Default `empty`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Image proxy

An HTTP or SOCKS5 proxy for downloading the images that requests link to. The gateway fetches them to count their tokens and to pass them on as data, and without a proxy the image hosts see this server's IP. With a Cloudflare Worker set, the proxy only carries the call to the Worker. Empty downloads directly.

Examples:

- `socks5://127.0.0.1:1080` Image downloads go through the local SOCKS5 proxy on port 1080.
- `http://proxy.internal:3128` Image downloads go through an HTTP proxy in the private network.

See also: [Cloudflare Worker image proxy](./gateway.md#CFWorkerImageUrl)

<a id="CFWorkerImageUrl"></a>

### Cloudflare Worker image proxy

Key `CFWorkerImageUrl` · Type url · Default `empty` · rarely changed

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Image proxy

A Cloudflare Worker that downloads the images requests link to, instead of this server. The gateway posts the image address and the Worker key to it and reads the image back, so the image hosts only see Cloudflare. It takes precedence over the image download proxy. Some image hosts refuse Cloudflare, and those images then fail. Empty uses no Worker.

Examples:

- `https://img-proxy.example.workers.dev` Every image linked in a request is fetched by that Worker.

See also: [Cloudflare Worker key](./gateway.md#CFWorkerImageKey) · [Image download proxy](./gateway.md#ChatImageRequestProxy)

<a id="CFWorkerImageKey"></a>

### Cloudflare Worker key

Key `CFWorkerImageKey` · Type secret · secret: never shown after saving · rarely changed

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Image proxy

The key sent to the Cloudflare Worker with every image download, for a Worker that checks one. Leave it empty when the Worker checks none or no Worker is set.

See also: [Cloudflare Worker image proxy](./gateway.md#CFWorkerImageUrl)

## Image storage

<a id="ImageStorageProvider"></a>

### Image storage

Key `ImageStorageProvider` · Type enum · Default `local`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Image storage

Where generated images are kept so a request that asks for an image URL gets a link. Gemini, Cloudflare Workers AI and Stability AI return image data only. Off answers with base64 instead: images endpoints give b64_json rather than url, and Gemini replies carry the whole image inline. A change applies at once on every node.

Values:

- `local` This gateway: Kept on this gateway for 1 hour under the server address, at most 5 downloads per link and 2 MB/s per download. Several nodes need Redis so every node can serve every link.
- `s3` S3 compatible: AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, MinIO, Backblaze B2 and other S3 compatible storage. Without a public URL, links are signed for 1 hour and the bucket can stay private. The gateway deletes no files: add a lifecycle rule in the storage console (for example 1 day).
- `alioss` Alibaba Cloud OSS: Links are signed and valid for 1 hour, so the bucket can stay private.
- `smms` SM.MS: Free image host; images are public.
- `imgur` Imgur: Free image host; images are public.
- `off` Off: Images come back as base64, and clients that only read the image URL get none.

See also: [Also store upstream image and video links](./gateway.md#ImageStorageRehostUpstream) · [Server address](./site.md#ServerAddress)

Guide: [deployment/storage.md](../deployment/storage.md)

<a id="ImageStorageRehostUpstream"></a>

### Also store upstream image and video links

Key `ImageStorageRehostUpstream` · Type bool · Default `true`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Image storage

Image and video links from upstreams are swapped for links on this site, which work where the upstream host is blocked. It covers image links from DALL·E, Flux and similar upstreams and from Midjourney tasks, and video links from Kling tasks. Images are fetched at once; a video is fetched on its first download and kept, up to 512 MB. A link that cannot be fetched is passed on as it is. When off, upstream links pass through.

See also: [Image storage](./gateway.md#ImageStorageProvider)

Guide: [deployment/storage.md](../deployment/storage.md)

<a id="ImageStorageS3Endpoint"></a>

### S3 endpoint

Key `ImageStorageS3Endpoint` · Type url · Default `empty`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Image storage

The S3 API address of the storage, without the bucket. Without a public URL, links point at <endpoint>/<bucket>/... and are signed.

Examples:

- `https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com` Cloudflare R2; the region is auto.
- `https://s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com` AWS S3 in Frankfurt; the region eu-central-1 is read from the address.

See also: [S3 region](./gateway.md#ImageStorageS3Region) · [S3 bucket](./gateway.md#ImageStorageS3BucketName) · [S3 public URL](./gateway.md#ImageStorageS3CDNURL)

Guide: [deployment/storage.md](../deployment/storage.md)

<a id="ImageStorageS3Region"></a>

### S3 region

Key `ImageStorageS3Region` · Type string · Default `empty`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Image storage

The region requests are signed for; usually left empty. Empty reads it from AWS, Backblaze B2 and Wasabi endpoints and uses auto for anything else, which is what Cloudflare R2 expects.

Examples:

- `us-east-1` Signs for us-east-1, for MinIO or another storage that expects a fixed region.

See also: [S3 endpoint](./gateway.md#ImageStorageS3Endpoint)

<a id="ImageStorageS3BucketName"></a>

### S3 bucket

Key `ImageStorageS3BucketName` · Type string · Default `empty`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Image storage

The bucket images are uploaded to. It can stay private unless a public URL is set.

See also: [S3 endpoint](./gateway.md#ImageStorageS3Endpoint) · [S3 public URL](./gateway.md#ImageStorageS3CDNURL)

<a id="ImageStorageS3AccessKeyId"></a>

### S3 access key ID

Key `ImageStorageS3AccessKeyId` · Type string · Default `empty`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Image storage

The ID of an access key that may write to the bucket; its secret goes in the next field.

See also: [S3 access key secret](./gateway.md#ImageStorageS3AccessKeySecret)

<a id="ImageStorageS3AccessKeySecret"></a>

### S3 access key secret

Key `ImageStorageS3AccessKeySecret` · Type secret · secret: never shown after saving

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Image storage

The secret of the S3 access key. It is stored encrypted when an encryption key is set, never shown again, and saving the field empty keeps the stored one.

See also: [S3 access key ID](./gateway.md#ImageStorageS3AccessKeyId)

<a id="ImageStorageS3CDNURL"></a>

### S3 public URL

Key `ImageStorageS3CDNURL` · Type url · Default `empty`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Image storage

A public address of the bucket or of a CDN in front of it; images then get plain public links under it. Empty gives links signed for 1 hour, and the bucket can stay private.

Examples:

- `https://img.example.com` Images get links under https://img.example.com/ that work as long as the file exists.

See also: [S3 endpoint](./gateway.md#ImageStorageS3Endpoint) · [S3 bucket](./gateway.md#ImageStorageS3BucketName)

<a id="ImageStorageS3ExpirationDays"></a>

### S3 Expires header

Key `ImageStorageS3ExpirationDays` · Type int · Unit days · Range 0– · Default `0` · rarely changed

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Image storage

Days written into the Expires header of each uploaded image, for caches and CDNs. It deletes nothing: use a lifecycle rule of the storage for that. 0 writes no header.

Examples:

- `1` An image uploaded today says it expires tomorrow; the file stays until a lifecycle rule removes it.
- `0` No Expires header.

See also: [S3 public URL](./gateway.md#ImageStorageS3CDNURL)

<a id="ImageStorageOSSEndpoint"></a>

### OSS endpoint

Key `ImageStorageOSSEndpoint` · Type string · Default `empty`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Image storage

The endpoint of the Alibaba Cloud OSS region the bucket is in.

Examples:

- `oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com` A bucket in Beijing; the region cn-beijing is read from the address.

See also: [OSS region](./gateway.md#ImageStorageOSSRegion) · [OSS bucket](./gateway.md#ImageStorageOSSBucketName)

<a id="ImageStorageOSSRegion"></a>

### OSS region

Key `ImageStorageOSSRegion` · Type string · Default `empty`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Image storage

The OSS region the bucket is in; usually left empty. Empty reads it from an endpoint of the form oss-<region>.aliyuncs.com; other endpoints (an internal or accelerated one) need it, or uploads fail.

Examples:

- `cn-hangzhou` Signs for Hangzhou, for an endpoint the region cannot be read from.

See also: [OSS endpoint](./gateway.md#ImageStorageOSSEndpoint)

<a id="ImageStorageOSSBucketName"></a>

### OSS bucket

Key `ImageStorageOSSBucketName` · Type string · Default `empty`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Image storage

The OSS bucket images are uploaded to; it can stay private, since links are signed.

See also: [OSS endpoint](./gateway.md#ImageStorageOSSEndpoint)

<a id="ImageStorageOSSAccessKeyId"></a>

### OSS AccessKey ID

Key `ImageStorageOSSAccessKeyId` · Type string · Default `empty`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Image storage

The AccessKey ID of a RAM user that may write to the bucket; its secret goes in the next field.

See also: [OSS AccessKey secret](./gateway.md#ImageStorageOSSAccessKeySecret)

<a id="ImageStorageOSSAccessKeySecret"></a>

### OSS AccessKey secret

Key `ImageStorageOSSAccessKeySecret` · Type secret · secret: never shown after saving

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Image storage

The AccessKey secret of the OSS user. It is stored encrypted when an encryption key is set, never shown again, and saving the field empty keeps the stored one.

See also: [OSS AccessKey ID](./gateway.md#ImageStorageOSSAccessKeyId)

<a id="ImageStorageSMMSSecret"></a>

### SM.MS API token

Key `ImageStorageSMMSSecret` · Type secret · secret: never shown after saving

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Image storage

The API token of your account on the free image host, used for uploads. Images there are public.

See also: [Image storage](./gateway.md#ImageStorageProvider)

<a id="ImageStorageImgurClientId"></a>

### Imgur client ID

Key `ImageStorageImgurClientId` · Type secret · secret: never shown after saving

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Image storage

The client ID of an application registered with Imgur, used for anonymous uploads. Images there are public.

See also: [Image storage](./gateway.md#ImageStorageProvider)

## Midjourney callback

<a id="MjNotifyEnabled"></a>

### Midjourney callbacks

Key `MjNotifyEnabled` · Type bool · Default `false`

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Midjourney callback

Passes the callback address (notifyHook) of a Midjourney task on to the upstream, which calls it when the task changes. The call comes from the upstream, not this site, so it carries the upstream's view of the task and tells the upstream the caller's address. When off, the address is dropped and callers poll the task status.

## Intake rules for new upstream models

<a id="ModelLibraryRulesEnabled"></a>

### Run the inclusion rules

Key `ModelLibraryRulesEnabled` · Type bool · Default `true` · rarely changed

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Intake rules for new upstream models

Runs the inclusion rules after each daily model library sync, so new releases join the catalog on their own. Edited on the Models page, Inclusion rules tab. Off, the library still syncs but nothing is added or retired automatically.

See also: [Apply the inclusion rules](./gateway.md#ModelLibraryRulesApply) · [Inclusion rules](./gateway.md#ModelLibraryRules)

<a id="ModelLibraryRulesApply"></a>

### Apply the inclusion rules

Key `ModelLibraryRulesApply` · Type bool · Default `false` · rarely changed

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Intake rules for new upstream models

Lets the inclusion rules change the catalog: on, they add and retire models and notify admins of what they did. Off is a dry run: they change nothing and only notify admins of what they would do. Edited on the Models page, Inclusion rules tab.

Examples:

- `false` A new Claude release is reported as "would be enabled"; the catalog stays as it is.
- `true` The same release joins the catalog enabled, and admins are told it was added.

See also: [Run the inclusion rules](./gateway.md#ModelLibraryRulesEnabled) · [Inclusion rules](./gateway.md#ModelLibraryRules)

<a id="ModelLibraryRules"></a>

### Inclusion rules

Key `ModelLibraryRules` · Type json · Default `empty` · rarely changed

Where: Platform settings › Gateway › Intake rules for new upstream models

The rules that decide which library models join the catalog and which catalog models are retired. They are saved as a JSON list and edited on the Models page, Inclusion rules tab. Rules are tried in order and the first one whose conditions all hold decides: enable, add disabled, leave out or retire. Conditions are labs, id patterns, release age, whether a channel can supply the model, deprecated, open weights and endpoints. Each model is decided once, so a model you remove is not added back. Empty uses the built-in rules; an empty list does nothing.

Examples:

- `[{"name":"Retire deprecated models","deprecated":true,"action":"retire"}]` Deprecated catalog models stop being listed but stay callable; nothing is added.
- `[{"name":"New Anthropic models","labs":["anthropic"],"released_within_days":60,"supplied":true,"action":"publish"}]` An Anthropic model released in the last 60 days that a channel offers joins the catalog enabled.
- `` The built-in rules: retire deprecated models, add previews disabled, enable recent models of the main labs, add other supplied models disabled.

See also: [Run the inclusion rules](./gateway.md#ModelLibraryRulesEnabled) · [Apply the inclusion rules](./gateway.md#ModelLibraryRulesApply) · [Intake rules for new upstream models](./gateway.md#SupplyIntakeRules)
